summary.technical_approach: Foundation Protocol 采用 graph-first 设计，将异构实体建模为图中的节点和关系，支持多方组织、事件驱动协作、经济原语、metering、receipts、settlement，以及 policy、provenance、audit。它定位为包裹和桥接现有协议，而不是替换已有工具协议。
summary.experiments: 摘要没有给出模型实验、benchmark 或部署规模数据。主要内容应是协议抽象、对象模型、工作流和安全/审计机制设计，而非可复现实验结果。
summary.authors_note: 作者来自 University of Technology and Design、City University of Hong Kong、Singapore Management University、Nanyang Technological University、Duke University、University of Illinois 等机构。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper proposes a coordination protocol layer for an agentic society, representing agents, tools, resources, humans, institutions, and organizations in a graph-first framework.
summary_en.importance: The contribution is a system-protocol and conceptual architecture rather than a model-training result. It focuses on identity, relationships, collaboration, metering, settlement, provenance, audit, and policy when many agents interact in real-world workflows.
summary_en.technical_approach: Foundation Protocol uses a graph-first abstraction for heterogeneous entities and relations. It supports native multi-party organization, event-based collaboration, economic primitives such as metering, receipts, and settlement, and first-class policy, provenance, and audit. It is designed to wrap and bridge existing protocols instead of replacing them.
summary_en.experiments: The abstract does not report model experiments, benchmarks, or deployment-scale results. The likely substance is protocol design, object modeling, workflow semantics, and safety/accountability mechanisms.
summary_en.authors_note: The authors are affiliated with University of Technology and Design, City University of Hong Kong, Singapore Management University, Nanyang Technological University, Duke University, University of Illinois, and related institutions.

recommendation.zh: 偏协议愿景，不是训练或模型论文；了解 agent 协作抽象即可，除非你在做多 Agent 基础设施。
recommendation.en: This is a protocol vision rather than a model paper; glance for agent coordination abstractions unless you build multi-agent infrastructure.

paper.title: One Sentence, One Drama: Personalized Short-Form Drama Generation via Multi-Agent Systems
paper.abstract: Existing approaches for digital short-drama production typically rely on one-shot LLM generated scripts and loosely coupled pipelines, which fail to satisfy three key requirements of short-drama generation: (1) narrative pacing, resulting in weak hooks, insufficient escalation, and unattractive endings; (2) spatial consistency, leading to drifting scene layouts and inconsistent character positions across clips; and (3) production-level quality control, requiring extensive manual review and corre

summary.core_problem: 现有短剧生成方法在叙事节奏、空间一致性和生产级质量控制上存在缺陷，一键生成完整短剧尚未实现。
summary.importance: 首次提出从单句到完整短剧的端到端多Agent框架，涵盖剧本创作到视觉生成全流程。
summary.technical_approach: 分层多Agent框架：（1）多Agent辩论式故事生成模块，确保短剧节奏和叙事连贯性；（2）3D基础的第一帧生成机制，建立共享空间布局。包含迭代精炼机制。
summary.experiments: 在短剧生成任务上验证，与现有LLM脚本生成方法对比叙事质量和空间一致性；未提供具体模型规模。
summary.authors_note: 清华大学、新加坡国立大学等机构。

summary_en.core_problem: Existing short-drama generation methods fail at narrative pacing, spatial consistency, and production-quality control; end-to-end short drama generation from a single sentence is unsolved.
summary_en.importance: First end-to-end multi-agent framework transforming a user's single-sentence idea into a fully produced short drama, covering scriptwriting to visual generation.
summary_en.technical_approach: Hierarchical multi-agent framework: (1) multi-agent debate-based story generation for pacing and coherence; (2) 3D-grounded first-frame generation for shared spatial layout. Includes iterative refinement.
summary_en.experiments: Validated on short drama generation tasks; compared narrative quality and spatial consistency against existing LLM script methods; no specific model sizes provided.
summary_en.authors_note: Tsinghua University, National University of Singapore, etc.

recommendation.zh: 多Agent在短剧创作领域的应用，框架设计有参考价值但属于特定领域应用，对LLM基座预训练无直接启发。
recommendation.en: Multi-agent application in short-drama generation; framework design is somewhat interesting but domain-specific, no direct insight for LLM foundation pretraining.

institutions: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

paper.title: LCGuard: Latent Communication Guard for Safe KV Sharing in Multi-Agent Systems
paper.abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems increasingly rely on intermediate communication to coordinate complex tasks. While most existing systems communicate through natural language, recent work shows that latent communication, particularly through transformer key-value (KV) caches, can improve efficiency and preserve richer task-relevant information. However, KV caches also encode contextual inputs, intermediate reasoning states, and agent-specific information, creating an opaque c

summary.core_problem: 在多 LLM agent 系统中，KV cache 作为隐式通信通道可能泄露上下文、推理状态和 agent 私有信息，论文试图在共享 KV 前做安全过滤。
summary.importance: 贡献类型是多 agent latent communication 的安全框架。它关注的不是传统文本消息过滤，而是表示层面的 KV cache 共享风险；这对使用 KV-cache 传递中间状态、做 agent 间加速或隐式协作的系统有参考意义。
summary.technical_approach: LCGuard 将共享 KV cache 视为 latent working memory，在缓存片段传输给其他 agent 前学习表示级变换。论文把敏感信息泄露操作化定义为 representation-level leakage，并试图通过变换降低隐私泄露，同时保留任务相关信息。摘要未给出具体损失、攻击模型、变换网络结构和保真度约束。
summary.experiments: 摘要未提供模型规模、使用的 LLM、agent 任务、攻击/探测器设置、泄露降低幅度或任务性能损失。只能确认其实验目标应是评估 KV latent communication 中的敏感信息泄露与 LCGuard 的防护效果。
summary.authors_note: 机构包括 Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute 和 IBM Research；主题位于 LLM 多 agent 系统、KV cache 通信和安全表示学习交叉处。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper addresses sensitive-information leakage when multi-agent LLM systems share KV caches as a latent communication channel.
summary_en.importance: The contribution is a safety framework for latent communication among LLM agents. Rather than filtering natural-language messages, it targets representation-level leakage through KV-cache artifacts, which is relevant to systems that share hidden states for efficiency or coordination.
summary_en.technical_approach: LCGuard treats shared KV caches as latent working memory and learns representation-level transformations before cache artifacts are transmitted across agents. It operationalizes sensitive-information leakage at the representation level and aims to suppress private content while preserving task-relevant information. The abstract does not specify the loss, threat model, transformation architecture, or fidelity constraint.
summary_en.experiments: The abstract does not report model sizes, LLM backbones, agent tasks, attack or probing setup, leakage reduction, or utility loss. The likely evaluation target is privacy leakage and task preservation under KV-based latent communication.
summary_en.authors_note: The work comes from Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute and IBM Research, at the intersection of LLM multi-agent systems, KV-cache communication, and safety-oriented representation learning.

recommendation.zh: 看威胁模型就够；KV 通信泄露是真问题，但若没有强 probe 和效用曲线，结论只能当弱信号。
recommendation.en: Read the threat model only; KV leakage is real, but without strong probes and utility curves the result is only a weak signal.

paper.title: Multi-agent Collaboration with State Management
paper.abstract: Recent advances in multi-agent systems have shown great potential for solving complex tasks. However, when multiple agents edit a shared codebase concurrently, their changes can silently conflict and inconsistent views lead to integration failures. Existing multi-agent systems address this through workspace isolation (e.g., one git worktree per agent), but this defers conflict resolution to a post-hoc merge step where recovery is expensive. In this paper, we propose STORM, i.e., STate-ORiented M

summary.core_problem: 多个 coding agent 并发编辑同一代码库时，隔离工作区会把冲突推迟到合并阶段，导致视图不一致和集成失败。
summary.importance: 贡献类型是 coding-agent 系统设计。它关注多 agent 协作中的状态一致性和写入时冲突处理，比简单多 agent 投票或分工更接近真实软件工程工作流。
summary.technical_approach: 提出 STORM，即 State-Oriented Management。系统作为共享 workspace 的中介，管理 agent 状态和写入操作，保证每个 agent 在一致代码视图上工作，并在写入时检测与解决冲突，而不是事后依赖 git worktree merge。
summary.experiments: 在 Commit0 和 PaperBench 上跨多个 LLM 评测。相对 git-worktree 多 agent baseline，STORM 在 Commit0-Lite 上提升 +18.7，在 PaperBench 上提升 +1.4，并报告成本效率相当或更好。
summary.authors_note: 作者来自 Shanghai Jiaotong University、Emory University 和 Peking University；工作面向多 agent 代码协作系统。

summary_en.core_problem: When multiple coding agents edit a shared repository concurrently, isolated workspaces defer conflicts to a late merge step, causing inconsistent views and integration failures.
summary_en.importance: This is a coding-agent systems contribution. It studies state consistency and write-time conflict handling in multi-agent software workflows, which is more realistic than simple agent voting or task decomposition.
summary_en.technical_approach: STORM mediates interactions with the shared workspace. It manages agent state, enforces consistent repository views, and detects or resolves conflicting edits at write time instead of relying on post-hoc git-worktree merging.
summary_en.experiments: The method is evaluated on Commit0 and PaperBench with multiple LLMs. It improves over a git-worktree-based multi-agent baseline by +18.7 on Commit0-Lite and +1.4 on PaperBench, with comparable or better cost efficiency.
summary_en.authors_note: The authors are from Shanghai Jiaotong University, Emory University, and Peking University; the work targets multi-agent coding collaboration systems.

recommendation.zh: 作为 coding-agent 系统备查即可；核心信号是写入时状态管理比事后 merge 更干净。
recommendation.en: Keep it as a coding-agent systems reference; the useful signal is that write-time state management is cleaner than post-hoc merging.

paper.title: ProCrit: Self-Elicited Multi-Perspective Reasoning with Critic-Guided Revision for Multimodal Sarcasm Detection
paper.abstract: Multimodal sarcasm detection requires reasoning over cross-modal incongruities between literal expression and intended meaning, yet the specific analytical perspectives needed vary across samples due to the diversity of sarcastic mechanisms. While recent methods make this analytical process explicit, they still rely on fixed, predefined perspectives that operate independently under hand-crafted routing rules. We argue that multimodal sarcasm detection instead calls for self-elicited multi-perspe

summary.core_problem: 多模态讽刺检测需要对跨模态不一致性进行推理，但现有方法依赖固定预定义视角和手工路由规则，无法适应不同样本的讽刺机制多样性。
summary.importance: 方法创新：提出了Proposal-Critique两agent框架，实现了自激发多视角推理与批评引导的修订，并合成了过程级推理标注数据。
summary.technical_approach: ProCrit 由 proposal agent（多视角推理）和 critic agent（外部评估与定向修订引导）组成，通过合成过程级推理标注解决缺乏过程监督的问题。
summary.experiments: 论文摘要未提供完整的实验结果细节，包括模型规模、baseline对比和量化指标。
summary.authors_note: 包含百度研究者，主要应用领域为多模态情感分析。

summary_en.core_problem: Multimodal sarcasm detection requires reasoning over cross-modal incongruities, but existing methods rely on fixed predefined perspectives with hand-crafted routing rules, failing to adapt to diverse sarcasm mechanisms across samples.
summary_en.importance: Methodological novelty: Proposal-Critic two-agent framework enabling self-elicited multi-perspective reasoning with critic-guided revision, plus synthesized process-level reasoning annotation data.
summary_en.technical_approach: ProCrit consists of a proposal agent for multi-perspective reasoning and a critic agent for external evaluation and targeted revision guidance, with synthesized process-level reasoning annotations to address lack of process supervision.
summary_en.experiments: Abstract does not provide complete experimental details including model size, baselines, or quantitative metrics.
summary_en.authors_note: Includes researchers from Baidu Inc., primarily focused on multimodal sentiment analysis.

recommendation.zh: 特定领域（讽刺检测）的多模态agent应用，方法属于现有agent范式的领域适配，对LLM基座研究无直接启发。
recommendation.en: Domain-specific multimodal agent application (sarcasm detection); adapts existing agent paradigms to a niche task with no direct insight for LLM foundation research.

paper.title: AgentCo-op: Retrieval-Based Synthesis of Interoperable Multi-Agent Workflows
paper.abstract: Designing multi-agent workflows is especially difficult in open-ended scientific settings where tasks lack curated training sets, reliable scalar evaluation metrics, and standardized interfaces between existing tools and agents. We propose AgentCo-op, a retrieval-based synthesis framework that composes reusable skills, tools, and external agents into executable workflows through typed artifact handoffs, then applies bounded self-guided local repair to implicated components when execution evidenc

summary.core_problem: 开放科学场景下设计多Agent工作流困难：缺乏标注训练集、可靠评估指标和标准化工具-Agent接口
summary.importance: 方法创新，提出基于检索的可互操作多Agent工作流合成框架
summary.technical_approach: AgentCo-op通过类型化制品交接组合可复用技能/工具/外部Agent为可执行工作流，执行失败时对受影响组件进行有界自引导局部修复
summary.experiments: 在两个基因组学案例研究（空间转录组学协作发现、单细胞多组学跨模态标记分析并行工作流）中验证了可行性，无量化SOTA对比
summary.authors_note: 卡内基梅隆大学计算生物学系，无知名作者

summary_en.core_problem: Designing multi-agent workflows in open-ended scientific settings is hard due to lack of curated training data, reliable evaluation metrics, and standardized tool-agent interfaces
summary_en.importance: Methodological innovation: a retrieval-based synthesis framework for composing interoperable multi-agent workflows
summary_en.technical_approach: AgentCo-op composes reusable skills, tools, and external agents into executable workflows via typed artifact handoffs, applying bounded self-guided local repair when execution evidence indicates failure
summary_en.experiments: Verified feasibility in two genomics case studies (spatial transcriptomics collaborative discovery, parallel cross-modality marker analysis on single-cell multiome data); no quantitative SOTA comparison
summary_en.authors_note: Carnegie Mellon University, Ray and Stephanie Lane Computational Biology Department, no notable authors

recommendation.zh: 科学计算领域的Multi-Agent架构探索，基于检索的工作流合成思路对Agent设计有微弱启发，无需深读
recommendation.en: Multi-agent architecture exploration for scientific computing; retrieval-based workflow synthesis provides minor insight for agent design, no deep read needed

institutions: Ray and Stephanie Lane Computational Biology Department

paper.title: STAR-PólyaMath: Multi-Agent Reasoning under Persistent Meta-Strategic Supervision
paper.abstract: Frontier AI models and multi-agent systems have led to significant improvements in mathematical reasoning. However, for problems requiring extended, long-horizon reasoning, existing systems continue to suffer from fundamental reliability issues: hallucination accumulation, memory fragmentation, and imbalanced reasoning-tool trade-offs. In this paper, we introduce STAR-PólyaMath, a multi-agent framework that systematically addresses these challenges through meta-level supervision and structured R

summary.core_problem: 现有多智能体数学推理系统在长程推理问题上存在三个根本缺陷：幻觉累积（中间推理错误沿长轨迹传播）、记忆碎片化（回溯时难以保留关键信息、或保留过多冗余上下文）、推理-工具权衡失衡（过度依赖代码搜索掩盖数学结构，缺乏元认知能力调整策略）。论文提出通过持续元策略监督来系统性解决这些问题。
summary.importance: 对预训练研究的启示主要在post-train和推理范式层面：(1) 长程推理的可靠性瓶颈可能不在模型知识本身，而在推理过程的结构化管理——这对RL训练中reward信号的设计（如何奖励结构化推理而非蛮力搜索）有参考价值；(2) 元策略监督作为一种训练-free的推理编排方案，其有效性暗示某些推理缺陷可通过更好的推理调度弥补，而非必须通过额外预训练或SFT；(3) 分离控制流与推理（用无推理能力的Python orchestrator做状态机控制）的架构设计对降低错误传播有实际意义。
summary.technical_approach: STAR-PólyaMath框架包含三个LLM角色：Reasoner（生成推理步骤）、Verifier（验证每一步正确性）、以及一个持续存在的Meta-Strategist（元策略师，在整个解题过程中保持全局监督，跨尝试维护策略记忆，发布元策略决策）。整个系统由无推理能力的Python orchestrator编排，通过显式状态机推进（包含嵌套的challenge-step-replan循环），将控制流与推理分离，通过回溯和重新规划限制错误传播。Reasoner和Verifier通过结构化双向辩论循环互动。
summary.experiments: 在多个竞赛数学基准上取得当前最佳成绩：AIME 2025、MathArena Apex Shortlist、MathArena Apex 2025、Putnam 2025、IMO 2025、AIME 2026、HMMT 2026年2月、USAMO 2026。最大优势在MathArena Apex 2025（93.75 vs. 最强基线GPT-5.5的80.21）。消融实验表明框架各组件均有独立贡献；将共享骨干替换为混合模型配置并未提升结果，说明收益来自编排框架而非模型选择本身。实验详细数据集和更多消融数字未在已读部分完全展示。
summary.reading_guide: 泛读建议：重点阅读§3方法部分的架构图（Figure 1）和状态机设计（challenge-step-replan嵌套循环）、Meta-Strategist的具体干预方式。实验结果部分关注跨基准的对比表和消融实验表。对预训练研究员，核心关注元策略监督如何通过结构化编排减少错误传播——这一原则可迁移到训练数据构造中。预计阅读时间20-25分钟。
summary.authors_note: 机构和作者信息未在已读部分明确给出。从框架复杂度和引用GPT-5.5作为基线来看，可能是业界研究团队。

summary_en.core_problem: Existing multi-agent mathematical reasoning systems suffer from three fundamental failure modes on long-horizon problems: hallucination accumulation (errors propagate along long solution trajectories), memory fragmentation (difficulty retaining salient information across backtracking attempts while avoiding excessive context), and imbalanced reasoning-tool trade-offs (over-reliance on brute-force code search obscures mathematical structure, lacking metacognition to revise strategy). This work introduces persistent meta-level supervision as a systematic remedy.
summary_en.importance: For pretraining research, the implications are primarily at the post-train and inference paradigm level: (1) Long-horizon reasoning reliability bottlenecks may lie in structured management of the inference process rather than model knowledge itself—this informs reward signal design in RL training (how to reward structured reasoning over brute-force search); (2) The effectiveness of training-free meta-strategic supervision suggests certain reasoning deficits can be mitigated through better inference orchestration without additional pretraining or SFT; (3) The separation of control flow from inference (a reasoning-free Python orchestrator managing a state machine) has practical implications for reducing error propagation.
summary_en.technical_approach: STAR-PólyaMath features three LLM roles: Reasoner (generates reasoning steps), Verifier (validates each step), and a persistent Meta-Strategist (maintains global oversight throughout the entire problem-solving process, retains strategic memory across attempts, issues meta-strategic decisions). A reasoning-free Python orchestrator coordinates the system via an explicit state machine with nested challenge-step-replan loops, separating control from inference and bounding error propagation through trace-back and re-planning. The Reasoner and Verifier interact through structured bidirectional debate loops.
summary_en.experiments: Achieves best-reported scores across AIME 2025, MathArena Apex Shortlist, MathArena Apex 2025, Putnam 2025, IMO 2025, AIME 2026, HMMT February 2026, and USAMO 2026. Largest margin on MathArena Apex 2025 (93.75 vs. 80.21 by the strongest baseline GPT-5.5). Ablation studies show each framework component contributes independently; swapping the shared backbone for mixed-model configurations does not improve results, indicating gains come from orchestration rather than model selection. Full experimental details and additional ablation numbers not fully available in the read sections.
summary_en.reading_guide: For skim-level reading: focus on §3 (Method) architecture diagram (Figure 1) and the state machine design (nested challenge-step-replan loops), plus the Meta-Strategist's specific intervention mechanisms. In results, examine the cross-benchmark comparison tables and ablation tables. For pretraining researchers, the key takeaway is how structured orchestration via meta-strategic supervision reduces error propagation—a principle transferable to training data construction. Estimated reading time: 20–25 minutes.
summary_en.authors_note: Institution and author information not explicitly provided in the read sections. Likely an industry research team given framework complexity and GPT-5.5 baseline reference.

recommendation.zh: 多智能体数学系统更像推理编排；可借鉴 trace-back/replan 设计，不必按预训练论文细读。
recommendation.en: This is reasoning orchestration more than pretraining; borrow the trace-back/replan design, but do not read it like a pretraining paper.

paper.title: AutoResearchClaw: Self-Reinforcing Autonomous Research with Human-AI Collaboration
paper.abstract: Automating scientific discovery requires more than generating papers from ideas. Real research is iterative: hypotheses are challenged from multiple perspectives, experiments fail and inform the next attempt, and lessons accumulate across cycles. Existing autonomous research systems often model this process as a linear pipeline: they rely on single-agent reasoning, stop when execution fails, and do not carry experience across runs. We present AutoResearchClaw, a multi-agent autonomous research p

summary.core_problem: 把自动化科研从一次性线性流水线，推进到能处理失败、积累经验并接受人类干预的多轮研究系统。
summary.importance: 贡献是通用 research agent 系统设计：它强调假设生成、实验执行、失败修复、结果核验、人类协作和跨轮记忆的闭环，而不是只让单个 agent 从 idea 生成论文。
summary.technical_approach: AutoResearchClaw 包含五个机制：结构化多 agent debate 用于假设生成和结果分析；带 Pivot/Refine 决策的 self-healing executor；可验证结果报告以减少编造数字和幻觉引用；七种人类干预模式；跨运行演化机制，把过去失败转为后续安全规则或策略经验。
summary.experiments: 摘要未给出具体 benchmark、任务数量、成功率、模型配置或与现有 autonomous research system 的量化对比。可确认的是论文强调真实研究循环中的失败恢复和跨 run 经验积累。
summary.authors_note: 机构列表包含 UNC-Chapel Hill、UC Santa Cruz、Carnegie Mellon University、NUS、UC Berkeley；题面标注涉及 Meta，但摘要作者机构细节不足以确认具体作者归属。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper aims to move autonomous research systems from one-shot linear pipelines toward iterative systems that handle failures, accumulate experience, and support human intervention.
summary_en.importance: It is a general research-agent system contribution. The focus is the full loop of hypothesis generation, execution, failure recovery, result verification, human collaboration, and cross-run memory rather than paper generation from a single idea.
summary_en.technical_approach: AutoResearchClaw uses five mechanisms: structured multi-agent debate for hypotheses and result analysis, a self-healing executor with Pivot/Refine decisions, verifiable result reporting to reduce fabricated numbers and hallucinated citations, seven modes of human intervention, and cross-run evolution that turns prior failures into future safeguards or strategies.
summary_en.experiments: The abstract does not specify benchmarks, task counts, success rates, model configurations, or quantitative comparisons against existing autonomous research systems. It does state that the system targets failure recovery and experience accumulation across research cycles.
summary_en.authors_note: The listed affiliations include UNC-Chapel Hill, UC Santa Cruz, Carnegie Mellon University, NUS, and UC Berkeley; the prompt notes Meta involvement, but the abstract does not provide enough detail to map specific authors to it.

recommendation.zh: 扫系统图和失败恢复设计即可；科研 agent 的关键不是多 agent 名字，而是结果可验证和跨 run 记忆是否真的闭环。
recommendation.en: Skim the system diagram and failure-recovery design; for research agents, the signal is verifiable results and real cross-run memory, not the multi-agent label.

Existing autonomous research systems often model this process as a linear pipeline: they rely on single-agent reasoning, stop when execution fails, and do not carry experience across runs. We present AutoResearchClaw, a multi-agent autonomous research p

recommendation.en: Keep it as a research-agent workflow reference; the components are sensible, but the abstract does not show clean ablations.

paper.title: TeamTR: Trust-Region Fine-Tuning for Multi-Agent LLM Coordination
paper.abstract: Multi-agent LLM systems have shown promise for complex reasoning, yet recent evaluations reveal they often underperform single-model baselines. We identify a structural failure mode in sequential fine-tuning of shared-context teams: updating one agent shifts the team's context distribution, and when subsequent updates are evaluated on cached rollouts, this mismatch compounds. We formalize this as the compounding occupancy shift and prove that stale-occupancy evaluation incurs a penalty that scal

summary.core_problem: 共享上下文的多智能体LLM系统在采用逐个智能体顺序微调时会出现复合占用偏移问题：前序智能体的更新会改变整个团队的上下文分布，后续智能体仍使用更新前缓存的轨迹做训练评估时，分布不匹配会随智能体数量累积，最终导致即使单个智能体更新局部收益为正，整体团队协调性能反而出现倒退。
summary.importance: 揭示了多智能体LLM微调中被忽略的训练过程缺陷，为模块化微调的稳定性设计提供了严格的理论依据，相关的占用偏移分析和信任域约束思路也可以迁移到持续预训练、多组件模型联合微调等存在分布偏移的场景。
summary.technical_approach: 首先将多智能体团队的交互建模为折扣MDP，共享上下文作为状态，智能体的消息作为动作；在轮流交互的协议下，证明了团队级的策略散度可以简化为单个智能体在访问状态上的散度，解决了联合动作空间信任域难以计算的问题。接着形式化定义复合占用偏移，从理论上证明：基于旧分布缓存轨迹的 stale-occupancy 评估带来的性能损失随智能体数量n呈二次方增长，而每次更新后重新采样轨迹的 intermediate-occupancy 评估可将损失降至随n线性增长。基于此提出TeamTR框架：每次更新单个智能体后都重新采样当前团队的轨迹，保证后续智能体在最新的上下文分布上训练，同时对每个智能体施加可通过token级KL散度监控的信任域约束，限制单次更新带来的分布漂移，最终给出每次更新后团队性能提升的严格下界证明，且该结论适用于任意智能体更新顺序。
summary.experiments: 论文通过对比实验验证TeamTR优于顺序微调基线，能够稳定多智能体团队的训练过程，同时支持组件的即插即用；理论部分给出了两种评估方式下损失随智能体数量的缩放关系，实验部分的具体数值未在已提供的论文片段中完整呈现。
summary.reading_guide: 重点阅读第3节的理论框架部分，理解复合占用偏移的形式化定义和两种评估方式的损失缩放证明；第4节的TeamTR算法细节，尤其是轮流协议下的散度分解和token级信任域约束的实现方式；泛读附录B.1的引理证明补充细节，全文预计阅读时间1.5-2小时。
summary.authors_note: 论文未提供完整作者和机构信息

summary_en.core_problem: Shared-context multi-agent LLM systems suffer from compounding occupancy shift during sequential per-agent fine-tuning: updates to earlier agents alter the team's overall context distribution, and subsequent agents trained on cached rollouts collected before these updates face accumulating distribution mismatch. This leads to degraded team coordination even when individual agent updates show positive local performance gains.
summary_en.importance: It identifies a previously overlooked training process flaw in multi-agent LLM fine-tuning and provides rigorous theoretical foundations for the stability of modular fine-tuning. The analysis of occupancy shift and trust region constraints can also be extended to scenarios with distribution shift such as continual pretraining and joint fine-tuning of multi-component models.
summary_en.technical_approach: First, multi-agent team interactions are modeled as a discounted MDP, with shared context as states and agent messages as actions. Under the turn-taking protocol, team-level policy divergence is proven to reduce to single-agent divergence on visited states, solving the intractability of trust regions over the joint action space. Compounding occupancy shift is then formalized, with theoretical proof that stale-occupancy evaluation (using cached old-distribution rollouts) incurs performance penalty scaling quadratically with the number of agents n, while intermediate-occupancy evaluation (resampling trajectories after each update) reduces this penalty to linear scaling. Based on these findings, the TeamTR framework is proposed: trajectories are resampled after each individual agent update to ensure subsequent agents train on the latest context distribution, and per-agent trust region constraints monitorable via token-level KL divergence are enforced to bound distribution drift from each update. Rigorous lower bounds for team performance improvement after each update are derived, applicable to any agent update order.
summary_en.experiments: Comparative experiments show TeamTR outperforms sequential fine-tuning baselines, stabilizes multi-agent team training, and supports plug-and-play of components. Theoretical sections provide the scaling relations of penalty with agent count for the two evaluation methods; full experimental metrics are not included in the provided paper excerpts.
summary_en.reading_guide: Focus on Section 3 for the theoretical framework, formal definition of compounding occupancy shift, and proof of penalty scaling for the two evaluation methods. Read Section 4 for details of the TeamTR algorithm, especially divergence factorization under turn-taking protocol and implementation of token-level trust region constraints. Skim Appendix B.1 for supplementary proof details. Estimated reading time is 1.5-2 hours.
summary_en.authors_note: Full author and affiliation information is not provided in the paper excerpts

recommendation.zh: 多智能体微调中的分布偏移问题分析，对理解 RL/SFT 在多轮交互中的训练动态有一定参考价值，可看其理论分析部分。
recommendation.en: Analysis of distribution shift in multi-agent fine-tuning, offers some reference value for understanding training dynamics of RL/SFT in multi-turn interactions, worth skimming the theoretical analysis.

This process requires substantial trial-and-error exploration, yet the resulting knowledge--resolved dependencies, repair strategies--stays trapped in a single conversation, unavailable to future agents. We therefore formulate repository bootstrapping as a reusable startup knowledge problem and introduce Bo
